meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Maybe I should take off my pants too?
Maybe you will put on a masterclass?

examples.text: А можно сделать шоу молекулярной кухни?
examples.trans: Can we do a molecular cuisine show?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'you'll help', paired with 'помогать'.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'корить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'conquer / win over'.

examples.text: Может быть, ты мне поможешь покорить её?

meanings.en: once, at one time in the past
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: У вас же когда-то любовь была.
examples.trans: After all, you two once had love.

examples.text: Твой отец когда-то назвал меня очкариком.
examples.trans: Your father once called me four-eyes.

examples.text: Мы когда-то жили в этой квартире.
examples.trans: We once lived in this flat.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'love' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У вас же когда-то любовь была.
examples.trans: After all, you two once had love.

examples.text: Первый раз я запел про любовь!
examples.trans: For the first time I sang of love!

examples.text: Марина, послушайте, это всё из-за любви!
examples.trans: Marina, listen, it's all because of love!

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'tell', paired with 'рассказывать'.

examples.trans: Tell me what happened.

meanings.en: to be needed, to become necessary
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'надобиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will be needed', paired with 'требоваться'.

examples.text: Этот ключ мне больше не понадобится.
examples.trans: I won't need this key anymore.
If you need help, tell me.

examples.text: Спасибо тебе, Марина. Этот ключ мне больше не понадобится.
examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. I won't need this key anymore.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.trans: I am not nervous at all.

examples.text: А это совсем не твоё дело.
examples.trans: That is none of your business at all.
Really, this is not yours at all?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dmitry Vladimirovich, please wake up.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That is, you give it only to yourself.

examples.text: Вика любит только дорогие подарки и украшения.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'рогой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('expensive').

examples.text: Вика любит только дорогие подарки и украшения.
examples.trans: Vika loves only expensive gifts and jewelry.

examples.text: Сказал, что Вика любит дорогие подарки.
examples.trans: You said that Vika loves expensive gifts.
Hello, dear guests!

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'арок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'gifts' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вика любит только дорогие подарки и украшения.
examples.trans: Vika loves only expensive gifts and jewelry.

examples.text: Подождите, так это подарок для Вики?

examples.text: Сказал, что Вика любит дорогие подарки.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'крашение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'jewelry' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вика любит только дорогие подарки и украшения.
examples.trans: Vika loves only expensive gifts and jewelry.

examples.text: Неправда, я оставил его для украшения.
examples.trans: Not true, I left it for decoration.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'статься'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'broke up', paired with 'расставаться'.

examples.trans: We will definitely break up.

examples.text: Нет, я всё решил! Мы с ней точно расстанемся.
examples.trans: No, I have decided everything! She and I will definitely break up.

meanings.en: to think it over, to give it a thought
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'think', paired with 'думать'.

examples.text: Подумайте, нужна ли вам вторая Кристина.
examples.trans: Think whether you need a second Kristina.
So you are leaving, have you thought it through well?
I'll think about it.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('needed').

examples.trans: Please, you need to get a good sleep.

examples.text: Подумайте, нужна ли вам вторая Кристина.
